summary: A search is a step in a window's history. src/model.rs: the history's stacks hold `Visit { location, search: Option<SavedSearch> }` (`SavedSearch { query, in_folder, contents }`); `navigate`, `back`/`forward` and `back_by`/`forward_by` take the search the window shows, and the steppers return `Option<Step { moved, search }>`. One private walk (`History::steps`) says where each step leads, and the lists (`back_list`/`forward_list`, now yielding `Visit`), `can_back`/`can_forward` and the steps themselves (`go`) are all made from it. Back from a search is one step, to the place it was made in, whether or not a visit is held for that place; a visit that is just what the window shows is passed over. `search_title(words)` is the one place the wording `Searching “words”` comes from. src/finder/mod.rs: `live_search`, `restore_search` and `show_step` are new; `navigate`, `go_up` and `reveal_in_place` hand the live search to the history before ending it; `go_back_by`/`go_forward_by` ask the history first and change nothing when there is no step; `select_in_results` selects and scrolls to the folder Back came from when the returned search first answers. src/finder/toolbar.rs: the tooltips, the buttons' enabled state, the right-press guard, the menus and each item's click-time check read the same lists of visits; a search is labelled by `search_label`, the window's title for it with words over forty characters cut short. docs/manual.md: the Toolbar table's Back, Forward row, a paragraph in Searching, and the Toolbar menus bullet.
changelog: Back and Forward now remember searches. Going somewhere else from a search, by opening a folder from the results, Show in Enclosing Folder, the sidebar, the path bar, Go to Folder or Enclosing Folder, keeps the search in the window's history, and Back returns to it: the same words, in This Computer or the folder, by Name or Contents, with the folder you came back from selected if it is one of the results. Search Only in This Folder is then on or off as that search had it. Back during a search now only ends the search and stays in its folder, where it used to go on to the place before as well, and Forward brings the search back. So from a folder opened from the results, Back leads to the results, then to the folder you searched from, then to the place before it. The Back button is enabled during a search even in a window that has been nowhere else, the Back and Forward menus list a search as Searching "text", and the tooltips name it, both with long words cut short. Forward with nowhere to go no longer ends a search. A search that comes back runs again with the kind and the Nushell filter chosen now, in relevance order. One ended with Escape or by emptying the search field is not kept.
behaviour_changes: Leaving a search for another place keeps it in the history: a folder opened from the results, Show in Enclosing Folder, the sidebar and the folder tree, the path bar, Go to Folder, Cmd+Up, Home/Recents/Trash, a folder dropped on a window with no folder, a folder-scoped Smart Folder, `fff show`, and `fff gui` or a second launch with a path. Back returns to it with the same words, scope (This Computer or the folder) and Name or Contents, and runs it again. This holds in Recents, the Trash and sent results as well as in folders (probed).

Back during a search only ends it and stays where it was made. It used to go on to the place before in the same press. Forward brings the search back. From a folder opened from the results: Back gives the results, then the folder searched from, then the place before; Forward retraces all three.

Getting to the place before a search takes one more Back press than it did, when the search was left by going somewhere. Several searches left in one folder each put that folder between them in Back's menu (search, folder, search, folder).

Back into results selects the folder the window came from, and scrolls to it, when it is one of the results. It is applied with the search's first answer; words typed before that are another search and start with nothing selected.
The Back button is enabled during any search, also in a window that has been nowhere else. Its tooltip then reads Back to “<folder>” and its menu lists that folder first.
Forward with nowhere to go no longer ends a search (keys, the mouse's forward button, the toolbar button).

Going to the folder a search was made in keeps the search one Back behind as well: Show in Enclosing Folder for a result in the folder the window shows, a click on that folder in the sidebar or the tree, Go to Folder with its path. These used only to end the search. They also clear what Forward led to, as going anywhere does.

Back and Forward menus list a search as Searching “text”, and the tooltips read Back to Searching “text” / Forward to Searching “text”. Words longer than forty characters are cut to their first forty and an ellipsis in both. Menu items count searches as steps, and an item acts only while that exact visit (place and search) is still that many steps away.

Returning to a search sets the scope and Name or Contents it had, and both stay that way for the next search typed: Search Only in "Folder name" is on after a search in the folder comes back and off after one in This Computer. Kind and the Nushell filter are the ones chosen now, and the results are in relevance order from the top.

Forward is enabled only when it leads to something other than what shows: a leftover step equal to what the window shows (a returned-to search ended with Escape) is not a step. The same goes for Back.
Opening a folder-scoped Smart Folder that is already showing leaves one step back to its folder, not a repeat of the search. Opening one from another search leaves that search one more step back.
Back or Forward from a search to another search (by Forward after the words were typed again, or by a menu item) ends the first and runs the second, even when both have the same words.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

The results' sort is not restored (optional in the plan). A search that comes back starts at Relevance; since sorted-search-results a sort can choose which items a cut list holds, so a sorted, cut list can come back as other items. The manual says the results are in relevance order.

Where the results were scrolled to is not kept. Only the folder Back came from is selected and scrolled to; a result selected before Show in Enclosing Folder is not selected again (the folder it is in is, when that is a result).

After Back, Back from a folder opened from the results (results, then the plain folder), nothing is selected in the folder. Before, one Back led to the folder with the folder left selected when it was directly inside.
Kind and the Nushell filter are not part of what is kept, by the plan. Two Smart Folders with the same words, folder and Name or Contents but different kinds count as one search to the history.

Searches ended with Escape, the field's clear button or New Folder are not recorded, by the plan. Neither is one replaced where it stands: other words typed, a Smart Folder with no folder, or `fff gui` with words only.
A tab moved to a new window still loses its history, as before.

The cut of long words in a label counts characters, not what a reader sees as one letter, so a mark that combines with the letter before it, or an emoji made of several characters, can be split at the cut.
Folder names are not cut in the menus and tooltips; a very long one still runs out, as history-menus left it.

Commit message and Changelog paragraph brought in line with the above: the scroll, the cut of long words, Search Only in This Folder following a search that comes back, and why a showing search ends before the one a step leads to begins.

notes:

How it was checked. With the src diff reverse-applied on the final commit all eleven UI tests fail for the brief's reasons (finder.rs: Back from the opened folder shows no search; Back during a search leaves Projects for the folder before; the scope and Name or Contents are not back; the same-folder search is gone; the Smart Folder's Back goes past its folder; the retyped words find Roadmap.md because Back had left the folder. controls.rs: the Back button does nothing during a search in a fresh window; Back's menu has no folder for a search and no Searching item. basics.rs: the query is empty after Back), and with it back the tree is clean. The unit tests cannot exist without the change. Sixteen mutations of the code, one at a time, against the lib's tests and tests/finder.rs and tests/controls.rs (the two that went unnoticed again with tests/basics.rs): thirteen failed a kept test (no selection kept for the results; not cleared by other words; the same-place filter gone from go_back_by; the field not given the words; the scope not restored; Name or Contents not restored; Forward ending a search with nowhere to go; go_up not handing over the search; reveal_in_place not handing it over; Back disabled by the plain stack; the click-time check comparing places only; the right-press guard off; `Step.moved` looking at the last stop only). Two failed none and now fail the two tests added in review (see review_fixes). One changes nothing a user can see (also handing the folder to select to location_changed when a search follows) and is left. The new and neighbouring UI tests pass under SEED 0, 1, 7, 42, 99 and 1234.

Probes, in throwaway tests that are deleted. Two and three Back or Forward presses with nothing settling in between (the window ends where single presses lead, with the right folder's items, not the folder left's). Column view, the gallery, a window with tabs. A search made in Recents and in sent results, there and back; the same results sent twice with a search in between (the leftover step is passed over). What was selected before a search is selected again after Back ends it, and again after Forward and Back. A Nushell filter on through Back and Forward (rows right every time; see Found, not fixed for the selection). And a random walk of 400 steps under each of ten seeds through the real window: going to folders, Recents, the Trash, Cmd+Up, reveal, sent results, a Smart Folder with and without a folder, words sent as `fff gui` sends them, Escape, the scope and Name/Contents chips, Back and Forward by key, by button and by menu item. After every Back or Forward the window's title was the first item the button's menu had listed, the press had changed what shows, a button with no menu did nothing, Forward after Back gave back the place, words, scope and Name/Contents, and a folder's rows were that folder's items. No step failed. I took ten pictures of my own (review-1 to review-10) and looked at the implementer's thirteen.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code says. (1) A Back or Forward press that does nothing, or leads somewhere other than the button says. Everything is made from one walk, `History::steps`: the steps taken (`go`), the lists for the menus and tooltips, and whether a button is enabled. The unit test goes through every history six actions deep and the random walk through 4,000 steps of the real window; `live_search()` after `restore_search` equals the `SavedSearch` restored (query trimmed both ways, scope and Name/Contents set outright), which is what the walk's skipping of repeats relies on. (2) The wrong search on screen after a step: one search's rows under another's words or scope, or a selection on an item the user didn't choose. `show_step` ends the showing search before it restores another, so `set_query` never returns early on equal words; no test held that, and one does now. The folder to select among the results is applied once, with the first answer, when the rows were empty until then (`set_query` drops them when no search was showing, and `show_step` sees to that), so it cannot land on rows someone has been working in; other words, Escape and going elsewhere all clear it in `set_query`. (3) A search or a setting lost without a word. Forward with nowhere to go leaves the search alone (the history is asked before anything ends); Back from a search is taken back by Forward; going anywhere keeps the search behind. What does change silently is the scope and Name/Contents after passing through an older search, since both are the tab's settings for the next search too: that was accepted in the plan, and the manual now says so.

For the briefs still to come.
- disabled-toolbar-buttons-look (lane-f, at work now): the two buttons' `.disabled(..)` in render_toolbar now read `back_to.is_none()` and `forward_to.is_none()`, where `back_to` / `forward_to` are the first of `history.back_list(live)` / `forward_list(live)` and also feed the tooltips. Back is enabled during any search, in a fresh window too, so a test that wants a Back with nowhere to go must not be searching. tests/controls.rs has three new tests: after back_and_forward_buttons, after back_and_forward_buttons_list_their_history and after a_history_menu_goes_only_where_it_says.
- live-search-results (lane-d, at work now): in run_search's answer, right after `this.rebuild_rows(cx)`, three lines take `select_in_results` and select and scroll to the folder Back came from. Keep them there; a search that runs again finds it None. `set_query` clears it beside `enter_results`. A search restored by Back or Forward starts through `set_query` like a typed one.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks (lane-g, at work now): `open_smart_folder`'s folder branch goes through `Finder::navigate`, which now hands the live search to the history before it ends it, so a Smart Folder opened from a search leaves that search one Back behind, and opened twice it is still one step (equal searches in one place count once). `end_search` also runs at the start of `show_step`, on every Back or Forward that leads somewhere, before `restore_search`. If you put Kind, Contents or the filter back when a search ends, a Smart Folder's search that Back returns to comes back without them: `SavedSearch` holds `query`, `in_folder` and `contents` only. Carry more in it if that matters (set in `live_search`, applied in `restore_search`), and remember that two visits with equal `SavedSearch`es in one place are one step.
- recent-searches: your plan records a search at the top of `open_entries` and of `reveal_in_place`, before `end_search`. Both now read `live_search()` first; keep that before your call or after it, but before `end_search`. `restore_search` sets the field and the words exactly as `open_request` does (`set_value`, then `set_query(.., true, ..)`), after setting `self.scope` and `self.search_contents`; if you factor out `search_for`, it can use it. Reset your recall index there as in `end_search`. Decide whether a search that Back returns to counts as recent; it wasn't typed.
- show-in-enclosing-folder-key: `reveal_in_place` keeps the live search in the history even when the result is in the folder the window shows (History::navigate pushes a visit for the same place when a search is live), so Back after Cmd+Return is the results again. back_returns_to_a_search_left_without_leaving_its_folder in tests/finder.rs drives the menu item; put your key's test beside it.
- restore-session-tabs: the history's stacks hold `Visit { location, search }` now, and its fields are private to src/model.rs. `History::last_folder()` should read `visit.location` there. Searches in a history are not saved anywhere.
- search-start-no-flash: a search that Back or Forward returns to starts in `set_query` from "no search showing", every time, and its rows are dropped there like a typed search's; the folder to select is applied in run_search's answer after `rebuild_rows`.
- empty-state-messages: `Finder::title()` returns what it did, now through `model::search_title`. A returned search in a folder that has gone shows the search's empty state while it shows and the folder's error after Back.
- column-pane-selection-by-path, view-switch-keeps-selection: in column view Back to a folder still selects nothing in the pane (seen in a probe; `load_listing` selects in `self.selection`, which the panes don't read). Step 4 of column-pane-selection-by-path's plan covers it. Back into results selects in the list the results use, in every view.
- split-active-pane, tab-drop-and-close, tab-bar-overflow: nothing to do; each pane and tab keeps its own history, with its searches.

Found, not fixed (there before, outside this brief).
- With a Nushell filter on, Back doesn't select the folder it left. The selection is made right after the rows are rebuilt, when the filter's run for the new rows has only started and the rows are still cut by the last run's answer, so the folder isn't among them. Probed for Back to a folder with a filter that keeps the folder (nothing selected; without the filter it is), on code this change doesn't touch; Back into results behaves the same way. The rows themselves are right once the run finishes.
- Disabled pill buttons are drawn like enabled ones (disabled-toolbar-buttons-look is at work on it), so that Back is enabled during a search shows only in its tooltip, menu and click.
- The system's window title is set only when the place changes, so during any search, typed or returned to, it reads the folder's name while the toolbar's title reads Searching ….
- `follow_moves` reloads the place under a live search without ending it.
- A folder with a very long name still runs out of a Back or Forward menu and off the window in a tooltip; only a search's words are cut.
- Ending a search rebuilds the rows from the listing of the place being left, just before the new place is listed. With a Nushell filter on, that starts a filter run that is replaced at once. It was so before; since this change the history has moved by then, so that run's working folder is the new place. Its answer is used only until the new listing replaces it.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows. No cfg-specific code, src/term, src/macos.rs or src/win.rs is touched or calls anything whose signature changed (grepped), and Cmd+[ and Cmd+] from the search field are tested as Ctrl here. On a Mac check once: search, open a folder from the results, Cmd+[ twice, Cmd+] twice. Alt+Left in the search field is word movement on a Mac and Back on Linux and Windows, as before. (b) Passing back through an older search changes Search Only in This Folder and Name or Contents for the next search typed. The plan accepted it and the manual says it; if it surprises in use, the place to change is `restore_search`. (c) The wording `Back to Searching “atlas”` reuses the window's title for a search. (d) A folder where several searches were left takes two Back presses per search to get out of backwards, and Back's menu shows the folder between them each time. That is what a search being a step means, and Finder does the same, but it is more presses than before. (e) After Back, Back from a folder opened out of the results, the folder shows with nothing selected. (f) Forty characters for a search's words in a label is my choice; `HISTORY_WORDS_SHOWN` in src/finder/toolbar.rs is the one place. (g) A returned search starts at Relevance, so a sorted, cut list can come back as other items, and the folder Back came from may then not be among them.
